sample.name: the S9 extension (protocol §19.2)
sample.rule: all 534 S8a comments that are not in the first S9 sample, screened in ascending order of comment id, every one of them; the same three criteria, two configuration-A judges per comment, new agents that did not see the first sample's judgments

generator: S9-extension aggregation step of the natural arm's workflow (not a repository script), in its D63 version; every derived field follows the rules below
privacy: ids, SHAs, categorical judgments, counts and checked model-written paraphrases only: no login, mention handle, e-mail address, URL, repository name, model identifier or verbatim comment, PR or issue text

correction.protocol: experiments/protocol.md §19.2 (clones that exist are reused and not fetched again), §15.6 and §16.4
correction.text: the 57 comments of repository 136202695, whose existing clone is over the per-repository cap, had failed fetch_over_the_caps without a check of what the clone holds. The D63 step examined them from the clone's objects with no fetch: 5 are judged in batch 17 (by two new judges, under the same rules; none qualifies); 1 fails criterion 2 (§16.4) instead; 51 still fail fetch_over_the_caps. Every count, kappa and rule text here is recomputed from the rows with the rules of the version it replaces; only the rows of these 6 comments changed. D63's count of 44 that lack a commit or the PR head reads 43 that lack both the reviewed commit and the PR head ref, plus the criterion-2 failure

families.note: formed again over both samples (§19.3 as D63 reads it); no comment of batch 17 qualifies, so no PR is added and no family, reserve or id changes

sample_manifest.use: the first S9 sample; the extension is the S8a pool (684) without it

extension_ids.rule: every S8a comment id not in the first sample, ascending (scripts/screen_aidev.py connect, build_funnel and draw_sample, unchanged)

fetch_record.use: per comment: batch, reachability, the walk to the first later commit of the PR head that touches the commented file, the commit used's S8a attribution, the diff file and its sha256, the S9 failures before judging; as the D63 step left it (its section d63_correction)

judgments.record_unit: one batch and one judge: 17 batches x 2 judges; 25 comments each in batches 1 to 16, 5 in batch 17 (D63)
judgments.canonical_form: json.dumps(records, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False), UTF-8 (the first sample's canonical form)
judgments.use: the raw judgments (judgment_records); every outcome here is recomputed from them and the fetch record, and equals the file's outcome for all 405 judged comments

d63_step.use: sha256 only: the D63 correction (see correction)

texts.use: not read here; the judges' text inputs (via the batches)

natural_tasks_index.use: the first sample's S10 outcomes: the accepted families of each repository (§19.3)

judges.kind: model agents; protocol §15.6 and §19.2 call for two independent configuration-A agents, new ones that do not see the first sample's judgments. Their outputs reached this step from the workflow as judge 1 and judge 2; model identifiers stay in private run records. Batch 17 (D63) was judged by two new judges, under the same rules
judges.inputs: the 17 batch files of the fetch record: per comment the pseudonymised comment text, diff hunk, PR title, linked issue title and body, and the pseudonymised diff of the commented file between original_commit_id and the first later commit of the PR head that touches it

testable_offline: unclear (observed twice, judge 2; not in the first sample's list)

judges.standing: model proposals, not human labels; queued for human coding

rules.judge_verdict: qualifies when the judge's request_type is behaviour_change or defect_report, its addressed is yes and its testable_offline is yes; fails otherwise
rules.qualifies: both judges' verdicts are qualifies; both commits were reachable in the S9 fetch: original_commit_id (in the clone and in the PR head's history) and the commit used, diff_commit, the first later commit of the PR head that touches the commented file; and the commit used is agent-attributed under the S8a rule of scripts/screen_aidev.py (the fetch record's attribution of that commit's AIDev pr_commits row)
rules.judged: a comment was judged only when its reviewed commit is reachable and in the PR head's history and a later commit of the PR head changes the commented file, with a non-empty diff (the fetch record's rule). The 129 comments that fail before judging have batch, judge_1, judge_2 and judges_agree null; the first sample, by contrast, judged its comments in repositories that could not be fetched without a diff. In the repository over the cap whose clone grew in S10 of the first sample, the 5 comments whose objects the clone already held were judged in batch 17, with no fetch (D63)
failure_reason: fetch_over_the_caps: the repository is over the 300,000,000-byte per-repository cap (§19.2: a clone that already exceeded it is not fetched into, and a clone that reaches it is stopped); the comment fails S9 before judging
commits_not_fetchable: the repository could not be fetched (its clone was refused); the comment fails S9 before judging

no_later_commit_changes_the_commented_file: no later commit of the PR head changes the commented file, so S9 criterion 2 fails (§16.4); the comment fails S9 before judging and enters the rejection ledger with §16.4's reason
addressing_commit_not_agent_attributed: the commit used is not agent-attributed under the S8a rule; the comment fails S9 with this reason whatever the judgments
judges_disagree: one verdict is qualifies and the other fails; the comment is excluded and counted separately, not as a failure
otherwise both verdicts fail, and the reason is the first failed condition in the order of the protocol's criteria: not_behaviour_change_or_defect, not_addressed, not_testable_offline
rules.failed_conditions: every condition not met, in the order commits_reachable, commit_agent_attributed, request_type, addressed, testable_offline; a judged condition is not met when at least one judge says so (the rule is a conjunction over both judges), so for a disagreement it lists what the dissenting judge rejected; commit_agent_attributed does not apply where no later commit touches the file. A comment that failed before judging lists commits_reachable (fetch_over_the_caps, commits_not_fetchable) or addressed (no_later_commit_changes_the_commented_file: criterion 2)
rules.judges_agree: the two judges' verdicts are the same; null for a comment that was not judged
rules.fetch_status: the repository's status in the fetch record: fetched, clone_failed or over_cap
rules.commits_reachable: original_commit_id is in the clone and in the PR head's history, and the commit used is in the clone; where no later commit touches the file, original_commit_id and the S7 later commit are (as for the first sample's one such comment); false where the repository could not be fetched, and false on every row that fails fetch_over_the_caps: in the repository whose existing clone is over the cap, a comment's objects were looked up in the clone with no fetch (D63), and the comments that fail there lack the reviewed commit and the PR head ref, or a blob of the commented file that the diff needs
rules.diff_status: ok: non-empty diff of the commented file between original_commit_id and diff_commit; empty: no later commit of the PR head changes the file, so there is no diff to judge; unavailable: not fetched, or (D63) not computable from the objects of a clone over the cap
rules.diff_commit: on every row whose PR head was walked to a result (419): the commit used, the first later commit of the PR head that touches the commented file, found by walking the PR head's history from original_commit_id along the ancestry path (the rule of the first sample's correction, D50); null when no later commit touches the file. diff_commit_agent_attributed: the S8a rule applied to that commit's AIDev pr_commits row (bot author account or agent co-author trailer); null when there is no commit. Absent on the 115 rows that fail fetch_over_the_caps or commits_not_fetchable (for 8 of them the D63 step's walk found the commit, but the diff would need a blob fetch; the fetch record has it). For 386 of the 405 judged comments it is the S7 later commit
rules.kappa: Cohen's kappa, (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e), with p_e from each judge's own marginals; request_type collapsed to behaviour_or_defect (behaviour_change, defect_report) versus other; addressed and testable_offline on their recorded categories, a value outside the first sample's lists added as a category (testable_offline unclear); over the 405 comments judged by both judges
rules.verification: for the 101 comments that at least one judge qualified, with every transport protocol disallowed (so nothing was fetched; each clone's apparent size was the same before and after): original_commit_id and diff_commit are commit objects in the bare clone, diff_commit descends from original_commit_id and is an ancestor of the PR head ref, which resolves to the fetch record's head, and the diff file matches its sha256 in the fetch record. Every outcome was recomputed from the raw judgments and the fetch record with these rules and equals the judgment file's preliminary outcome
rules.s11_families: protocol §19.3 with §15.6 and §17.3, over the qualifying comments of both samples. The first sample's families and reserves NP-01 to NP-25 keep their ids, roles and places; a repository's accepted families are its S11 tasks in data/manifests/natural_tasks_index.json. A repository with 2 accepted families gets no new family. Elsewhere the new qualifying PRs of the repository (those not among the first sample's families and reserves), by creation time (AIDev pull_request created_at, then the lowest PR id), fill its open places (2 minus its accepted families) as families, each with its earliest qualifying comment (AIDev created_at, then the lowest id) as its correction and the others recorded; the next ones are its reserves (§17.3), used in order when a new family of the repository is rejected at S10 (a reserve takes the place of a family of its own sample only: the first sample's rejected families leave open places, which the new families fill, and the first sample's reserves take only the first sample's families' places). Ids: the new families from NP-26 in order of PR creation time (S10 takes them in that order), then the reserves in the same order. A first-sample PR with qualifying comments in the extension keeps its id, role and correction; those comments are its other qualifying comments. Applied before S10; formed again after the D63 correction, which added no qualifying comment

paraphrase_policy.stored: only for qualifying comments: judge 1's requirement_paraphrase, after the checks below; null otherwise, and null where judge 1's paraphrase fails a check (no other paraphrase is substituted)
checks: no login: whole-word, case-insensitive match against the logins of every participant of the sampled PRs (PR authors, review-comment authors on those PRs, linked-issue authors, commit authors and committers) and the repositories' owner names, read from the AIDev files in memory only
no mention handle and no e-mail address (the patterns of scripts/scan_tracked_files.py)
no URL and no domain name
no quoted text: no quotation marks or backticks, and no run of 6 or more consecutive words shared with the raw review comment, PR title, PR body, linked issue title or issue body
no pseudonymisation placeholder (role label or removed-address marker)
no name of a sampled repository (its owner or repository name, as a whole word, case-insensitive): an addition to the first sample's checks, which the first sample's 31 stored paraphrases also pass
no model identifier (the patterns of the S9 correction step and of the extension's judgment step)
paraphrase_policy.logins: the participants of the PRs of both samples (PR authors, review-comment authors on those PRs, linked-issue authors, commit authors and committers, with and without a [bot] suffix) and the repositories' owner names: 289 names, read from the AIDev files in memory only
paraphrase_policy.calibration: the same checks, run on the first sample's 31 stored paraphrases, pass all of them and give the longest shared word run recorded for each
paraphrase_policy.result: 89 of 91 paraphrases passed; longest shared word run among them 5; 2 failed and are not stored (caveats)

qualifying_rate.note: model proposals, not human coding; Wilson score intervals

s11_families.standing: planned before S10 of the extension; S10 can lower the number of accepted tasks but not raise it. A family that S10 rejects is replaced by the next reserve of its repository and of its own sample by creation time (§17.3), still with at most 2 accepted families per repository; building stops at 30 accepted tasks in all, or when every family of both samples has been processed (§19.5). Formed again after the D63 correction, which adds no qualifying comment: the families, reserves and their ids are the ones formed before it

agreement.population: the 405 comments judged by both judges (every comment of the 17 batches; batch 17: D63). The 129 comments that failed S9 before judging have no judgments and are not included; the first sample's kappa also counted its 19 comments whose repositories could not be fetched, which were judged without a diff

secondary.note: not requested by the protocol; reported for reading the main values

commits_reachable_only.note: every judged comment's commits were reachable, so these values equal the main ones

caveats.text: 129 comments were not judged and fail S9 with the fetch record's reason. fetch_over_the_caps (59, 2 repositories): one repository's existing clone was already over the 300,000,000-byte cap, because it grew in S10 of the first sample (the repository of the first sample's NP-07 and NP-08; 57 comments on 26 PRs), so nothing was fetched there. Its comments were first failed without a check of what the clone holds; after the D63 correction 5 are judged (batch 17), 1 fails criterion 2 (below) and 51 still fail here, 8 because the diff would need a blob fetch and 43 because the clone holds neither the reviewed commit nor the PR head ref (see the caveat on D63). Another repository went over the cap during its clone, as in the first sample (8 comments). commits_not_fetchable (56, 3 repositories): the clone was refused (HTTP 401 through the session's git proxy), as in the first sample. no_later_commit_changes_the_commented_file (14): no later commit of the PR head changes the commented file, so criterion 2 cannot hold (§16.4). The first sample judged its comments in repositories that could not be fetched without a diff and recorded its 2 over-cap comments as commits_not_fetchable (fetch_status over_cap); the extension judged only comments with a diff, as the fetch record's rule says, and gives the cap its own reason, the one §19.2 names

the commit used (the first later commit of the PR head that touches the commented file, at ancestry position 3) is not agent-attributed under the S8a rule: no bot author and no agent co-author trailer. The comment fails with addressing_commit_not_agent_attributed whatever the judgments; both judges call it refactor_design with addressed unclear, so it would fail anyway

caveats.topic: testable_offline value outside the first sample's categories
caveats.text: judge 2 answered testable_offline 'unclear' for these comments, a value outside the first sample's category list (yes, no, na). It is recorded as given and is not 'yes', so that judge's verdict fails; both judges say addressed 'no', so the comments fail on not_addressed in any case. The kappa for testable_offline counts 'unclear' as a fourth category

caveats.topic: commit used is a merge commit
caveats.text: the first later commit touching the file is a merge commit (agent-attributed through its bot author); its diff shows what the merge brought into the commented file, which may not be the agent's response to the review. S10's merge rule (§15.6) decides on such a task when it is built

caveats.topic: commit used is not the S7 later commit
caveats.text: for these comments the first later commit that touches the commented file is not the S7 later commit (the PR's next listed commit); the judges saw the diff to the first touching commit, as criterion 2 and the correction of D50 require, and that commit is the one used here

caveats.topic: two lines of history before the commit used
caveats.text: the fetch record notes that two lines leave the reviewed commit before the first touching commit (pr_line_is_a_line_up_to_first_touching_commit false); for one PR it was checked by hand that the first touching commit is a direct child of the reviewed commit
the batch diff was cut to its first 12,000 characters, so the judges saw part of the change

caveats.topic: file deleted or created by the commit used
caveats.text: the commit used deletes the commented file, or the file is absent on one side, so the diff shows the whole file removed or added (fetch record problems)

the texts of these comments had model identifiers replaced by a placeholder in s9x_texts.jsonl and the batches (fetch record texts.model_identifier_masking), so the judges saw the masked text; a task built from such a text must mask them again, since no model identifier is written into any file

2 qualifying comments have no stored paraphrase: judge 1's paraphrase failed a check (shared_word_run: a run of 6 consecutive words shared with a source text; repository_name: a word that is the name of the comment's own repository, which both judges' paraphrases use). No other paraphrase is substituted; the judgments are unchanged

caveats.topic: first-sample PRs with qualifying comments in the extension
caveats.text: 12 PRs of the first sample's families and reserves have qualifying comments in the extension. They keep their first-sample ids, roles and corrections (§19.3), and the extension's comments are their other qualifying comments. For 6 of them an extension comment was created before the first-sample correction; read over both samples, §15.6 would have made it the correction, but the first sample's families keep their places (§19.3), and the accepted ones are built

caveats.topic: families of repositories whose first-sample families S10 rejected
caveats.text: new families fill the open places of repositories whose first-sample families were all rejected at S10, some for reasons that hold for the whole repository (its test tooling, a submodule, a generated version module); S10 decides on each new family as on any other

caveats.topic: D63: comments of the over-cap repository examined from its clone's objects
caveats.text: the 57 comments of repository 136202695 had all failed fetch_over_the_caps without a check of what its existing clone holds, although §19.2 reuses existing clones (D63, 'A deviation, corrected'). The D63 step examined each from the clone's objects with no fetch of any kind: the comments whose PR head ref, reviewed commit, first later commit that changes the commented file and both blobs of that file are in the clone were diffed with the extension's own code and judged in batch 17 by two new judges, under the same rules (none qualifies); one has its PR head ref and reviewed commit in the clone, and no later commit on its PR head changes the commented file, so it fails criterion 2 (§16.4) instead; the others still fail fetch_over_the_caps, the fetch record giving what the clone lacks. D63's count of 44 that lack a commit or the PR head reads 43 that lack both the reviewed commit and the PR head ref, plus this criterion-2 failure. Their fetch_status stays over_cap, the repository's status

the judgments are model proposals, not human labels, and are queued for human coding (protocol §15.6). The judges were new agents that did not see the first sample's judgments (§19.2). S10 and the stop at 30 tasks are not applied here; summary.s11_families is the plan of §19.3 before S10

rows.requirement_paraphrase: The cache directory should be derived from the resolved working path after it is set, rather than from the default runtime root.
Converting expressions with undefined symbols to C++ should always fail with a clear exception, with no option to substitute placeholders.
Generating array offset expressions that contain undefined symbols should fail with a clear exception instead of emitting a placeholder.
Generating the sample program for array arguments should work without passing the removed undefined-symbol option, which the converter no longer accepts.
The heap-allocation warning for variable-length arrays should format the size without the removed undefined-symbol option, so generation does not crash.
The warning for stack arrays exceeding the maximum stack size should format the size without the removed undefined-symbol option, avoiding a crash.
Heap array allocation code should convert the array size without the removed undefined-symbol option, so code generation does not crash.
Zero-initialisation of heap arrays should convert the array size without the removed undefined-symbol option, so code generation does not crash.
Declaring zero-initialised register arrays should convert the size without the removed undefined-symbol option, so code generation does not crash.
Declaring register arrays should convert the size without the removed undefined-symbol option, so code generation does not crash.
Allocating thread-local arrays inside the parallel section should convert the size without the removed undefined-symbol option, so generation does not crash.
Zero-initialisation of thread-local arrays should convert the size without the removed undefined-symbol option, so code generation does not crash.
Applying the start offset to thread-local arrays should convert the offset without the removed undefined-symbol option, so generation does not crash.
Deallocating arrays with a nonzero start offset should convert the offset without the removed undefined-symbol option, so generation does not crash.
State propagation should return right after running the propagation pass, without also executing the legacy traversal code.
The markdown report should list all assignees of an issue rather than only the first one.
The class name derived from the project name should always be a valid Python class identifier.
When the derived class name is not a valid Python identifier, creation should fail with an error instead of substituting default names.
The returned publish information should distinguish items published in this deployment from items that already existed in the workspace.
The site lookup request should ask for up to 500 sites per page rather than 50.
When a record is skipped because its cached address is unchanged, the log message should also include that address.
The retry helper should keep polling long-running operations without a maximum attempt limit until an end state, logging only the current attempt.
The provider should accept an optional region prefix in the access identifier to choose the service endpoint, using the current default region otherwise.
The function-to-node factory should take the context storage key as its own parameter, and generated node constructors should no longer accept it.
The MCP tool factory should take the context storage key as its own parameter, and generated tool node constructors should no longer accept it.
Errors while reading a package initializer file during namespace discovery should be logged at error level instead of debug level.
Namespace discovery should also skip directories named in the shared exclusion set, such as samples, docs and test folders, while walking the package.
Accessing a lazily imported optional class whose dependency is missing should raise the original import error rather than an attribute error.
The red-team subpackage should import its classes eagerly again, printing an install hint if the optional dependency is missing, instead of lazy loading.
Importing the red-team subpackage without its optional dependency should raise an import error carrying the install hint instead of printing it.
The provider request helper should return None whenever the API reply status code is not the success code, instead of the raw response.
When the provider validates its configuration, it should log a warning that its implementation is still pending verification.
When creating a DNS record, the domain parameter sent to the API should be the main domain rather than the zone identifier.
If an account identifier is configured, the provider should log a warning that only the API key is required.
When listing DNS records, the domain parameter sent to the API should be the main domain rather than the zone identifier.
Record creation must send the fully qualified domain, built from subdomain and main domain, as the record name instead of the bare subdomain.
The record lookup should filter acceleration domains by domain name instead of filtering DNS records by record name and type.
The record lookup should read the acceleration-domain list from the API response and return the entry whose domain name matches.
For multiple configurations, each configuration's log level, when set, should be applied to the logger inside the loop before that configuration runs.
While running each configuration, the program should log which DNS provider that configuration uses.
Configuration files whose top level is a plain JSON array should no longer be accepted as a multi-configuration format.
Loading a configuration file whose top level is a JSON array should no longer be supported as a way to define multiple configurations.
The credential-embedded request URL should use the scheme and host of the provider's configured endpoint rather than a hardcoded host.
Configuration files with a top-level configs array should no longer be expanded into multiple configurations, as that format is unsupported.
Provider validation should explicitly reject an endpoint that lacks a scheme separator, raising a clear error.
With a providers list present, a null top-level dns value should be accepted rather than raising the providers-dns conflict error.
The request helper should drop the single-proxy parameter and take proxy configuration only through the proxy list parameter.
When the HTTP request fails, the provider helper should propagate the original exception instead of wrapping it in a generic runtime error.
An SSL setting given on the command line, even a false value, should take precedence over the environment setting, defaulting to auto.
When loading a remote config fails with a non-200 status, an error message should go to the error stream; success should print nothing.
A proxy setting present in the command-line configuration, even if empty, should take precedence over the environment's proxy setting.
When a remote config request returns a non-200 status, the error output should also include the response body.
Using the legacy expansion call form that passes the graph and the state should emit a deprecation warning.
When no configuration file path is given, the task manager should not substitute a default configuration file path.
When no configuration file path is given, the task manager should not substitute a default configuration file path.
When no log file path is given, the task manager should leave it unset rather than defaulting to a log file name.
With a claims challenge, the CLI credential's token-info call should raise an unavailable error carrying the reworded message: token retrieval failed, run az login.
With a claims challenge, the async CLI credential's get-token call should raise an unavailable error carrying the reworded message: token retrieval failed, run az login.
With a claims challenge, the async CLI credential's token-info call should raise an unavailable error carrying the reworded message: token retrieval failed, run az login.
With a claims challenge in options, the PowerShell credential's shared token path should raise an error carrying the reworded message: token retrieval failed, run Connect-AzAccount.
With a claims challenge, the async PowerShell credential's get-token call should raise an error carrying the reworded message: token retrieval failed, run Connect-AzAccount.
With a claims challenge, the async PowerShell credential's token-info call should raise an error carrying the reworded message: token retrieval failed, run Connect-AzAccount.
When a claims challenge triggers the error, the suggested login command in the message should also include the requested scope.
The IPv6 public address fallback list should contact its last lookup service over plain HTTP rather than HTTPS.
LLM node warnings, including the duplicate system message warning, should be emitted on a logger named Node.LLM instead of LLM.
The warning for a model given both as argument and class attribute should be emitted on the Node.LLM logger, not LLM.
Error responses should report the OpenAI-style error code in the code field and not add a separate error_code field.
Importing the package should fail when a required dependency is missing, instead of warning and exposing only the logging helpers.
Every template entry in the parameter file must include the enabled field, and validation should reject entries that omit it.
The embedding client should use the service endpoint followed by the version-one API path as its base address, instead of a deployment-specific path.
The document-preparation client setup should build clients whose base address is the service endpoint followed by the version-one API path.
Unit quantities and uncertain values should serialise through dedicated encoders to the standard dtype-and-data dictionary form and decode back.
The main conversion class should gain an instance method holding the grouped-pinyin logic, with the module-level grouped function delegating to it.
Add a lazy grouped method, analogous to the lazy conversion method, returning each word's pinyin as a single string instead of a list.
Provide a module-level lazy variant of the grouped conversion function, modelled on the existing lazy conversion function.
Add an instance method paired with the grouped method that returns each word's pinyin as one string rather than a list of readings.
The squared spectral norm method should accept its iteration limit, tolerance and verbosity options only as keyword arguments.
The combined post-plot adjustment function should accept the lower y-limit value through a keyword argument named ylow.
The combined adjustment function should take the legend and anchored-text overlap tolerances as keyword arguments named legend_otol and yscale_otol.
When converting chat-format content for responses requests, text items should be converted to the input-text type while keeping their text.
The event page model should provide a method that uses a given client to fetch the following page, returning nothing when no pages remain.
The extra-data mapping must keep reading the expiration value from its original field name in the provider's response.
The threshold separating absolute timestamps from relative expiry seconds should exceed one year, so year-long relative expiries are not mistaken for timestamps.
The new search path setting should be read from its default environment variable, without the extra alias names.
Authentication validation should treat empty-string token, client ID, or client secret values as not provided.
If the supplied automation definition fails schema validation during an update, the command should exit with a message reporting a validation failure.
The events client should always request the project's websocket subprotocol when connecting, whether or not an authentication token is configured.
After connecting, the events client should always send an authentication message carrying its token, even when no auth string is configured.
